unit:request-correlation.title: Integrate opt-in request correlation
unit:request-correlation.objective: Integrate opt-in configuration, request identity, response propagation, focused tests, and public documentation without claiming implementation or runtime success.

outcomes.statement: The planned integration preserves or securely generates one request ID, exposes it as req.id, and emits the same X-Request-Id value when enabled.
The planned integration leaves default request and response behavior unchanged when correlation IDs are not enabled.
The planned public surface is covered by focused tests and documentation.

criteria.statement: When enabled, each request exposes req.id and returns the same X-Request-Id, preserving a valid incoming value or generating one.
Existing applications that do not enable correlation IDs retain current request and response behavior.
The public configuration and request property are documented with focused tests.

expectedBenefits: Explicit ownership for configuration, request, response, tests, and documentation
Independent proof obligations for each registered strategy
expectedCosts: Requires integration of two explicit cross-module seams

integration.objective: Verify the exact integrated candidate across opt-in configuration, request identity, X-Request-Id response propagation, tests, and documentation.

unit:configuration.title: Define opt-in configuration
unit:configuration.objective: Plan the application-owned opt-in setting and preserve the disabled baseline and middleware compatibility.

outcomes.statement: Correlation IDs are controlled by explicit application configuration and remain disabled by default.

criteria.statement: The configuration is opt-in and disabled applications preserve existing behavior.

expectedBenefits: Isolates default-compatibility policy in the application owner

unit:request-identity.title: Resolve request identity
unit:request-identity.objective: Plan request-owned preservation of a valid incoming X-Request-Id or generation with a secure Node.js platform primitive, exposing the result as req.id without a runtime dependency.

outcomes.statement: An enabled request resolves one stable ID from a valid incoming header or a secure platform-generated value and exposes it as req.id.

criteria.statement: Enabled requests expose the preserved or securely generated request ID as req.id.

expectedBenefits: Keeps request identity semantics with the public request prototype

unit:response-propagation.title: Propagate the response header
unit:response-propagation.objective: Plan response-owned emission of the exact resolved request identity as X-Request-Id while preserving existing response behavior when disabled.

outcomes.statement: Enabled responses emit X-Request-Id with the same value resolved for req.id.

criteria.statement: The response returns the same X-Request-Id value exposed by the enabled request.

expectedBenefits: Makes response propagation independently testable at its owning module

unit:focused-tests.title: Add focused correlation tests
unit:focused-tests.objective: Plan focused request and response tests for incoming preservation, secure generation behavior, req.id/header equality, opt-in behavior, and disabled baselines.

outcomes.statement: Focused executable cases cover request identity, response propagation, and negative controls for disabled applications.

criteria.statement: Focused executable tests demonstrate the enabled request-ID behavior and its negative controls.

expectedBenefits: Centralizes focused behavioral proof while preserving one owner per test file

unit:public-docs.title: Document the public opt-in surface
unit:public-docs.objective: Plan public documentation for enabling correlation IDs, reading req.id, preserving incoming X-Request-Id, generated identifiers, response propagation, and unchanged defaults.

outcomes.statement: The public configuration and req.id behavior are documented as opt-in, including incoming and generated ID behavior.

criteria.statement: The public configuration and request property are documented.

expectedBenefits: Keeps the public contract explicit and statically inspectable

seam:configuration-to-request.specification: The request identity behavior reads the application-owned correlation-ID setting and remains inactive unless that setting is enabled.

semanticFacts.disabledBehavior: no request ID behavior is introduced by default

rules: Disabled applications retain existing request and response behavior
No runtime dependency is added

seam:request-to-response.specification: Response propagation uses the exact stable identity resolved for req.id and emits it as X-Request-Id only for enabled correlation behavior.

semanticFacts.identityRule: the request property and response header carry the same value

rules: Do not emit correlation behavior when disabled
Preserve a valid incoming X-Request-Id
Use a secure platform primitive when generation is required

advisoryFindings.message: The supplied request evidence shows generic header access but does not define which incoming X-Request-Id values are valid; the focused deterministic tests should encode accepted and rejected boundary cases without expanding the public contract implicitly.
